overview: Anglo American is a London-listed, globally diversified mining group undergoing a major portfolio simplification. Its retained, continuing-operations core is copper (Chile, Peru), premium iron ore (South Africa's Kumba, Brazil's Minas-Rio), manganese (Samancor JV) and the Woodsmith/Sakatti crop-nutrients growth projects, with De Beers diamonds still consolidated as an exiting business pending sale, while Steelmaking Coal (sold to Dhilmar, completion expected Q1 2027) and Nickel (agreed sale to MMG, pending EU antitrust clearance) are discontinued operations and Platinum Group Metals was already demerged as Valterra Platinum in May 2025. The company has also agreed a transformational merger of equals with Teck Resources to form 'Anglo Teck', a copper-focused global metals and minerals champion expected to complete by March 2027, after surviving a hostile approach/takeover interest from BHP in 2024 and renewed BHP interest in late 2025 that did not proceed.

business_model.summary: Anglo American extracts, processes and markets bulk and base metals/minerals, selling largely into global commodity markets at prevailing benchmark or index-linked prices (LME copper, iron ore indices, diamond price index), so revenue is transactional/cyclical rather than recurring, with no long-term fixed-price contracts for the bulk of volumes. Profitability is driven by production volumes, ore grades, unit costs and realized commodity prices rather than by customer relationships. The group is mid-way through a multi-year portfolio simplification (divesting PGMs, Steelmaking Coal, Nickel and De Beers) to concentrate capital in copper, premium iron ore, manganese and crop nutrients (Woodsmith polyhalite), and is about to combine with Teck Resources to materially increase copper scale and exposure (>70% of combined EBITDA from copper, per management).

revenue_streams.name: Copper (Chile - Collahuasi, Los Bronces, El Soldado; Peru - Quellaveco)
Premium Iron Ore (Kumba - South Africa; Minas-Rio - Brazil)

business_model.customer_type: B2B - global commodity trading houses, smelters/refiners, steelmakers, diamond manufacturers/retailers and industrial consumers; no meaningful retail/consumer exposure
business_model.geographic_mix: Operations concentrated in Chile and Peru (copper), South Africa and Brazil (iron ore, manganese), Southern Africa/Botswana/Namibia/Canada (De Beers diamonds), Australia (steelmaking coal, exiting) and the UK (Woodsmith project, corporate HQ); roughly half of employees are in South Africa and other Africa

competitive_position.market_position: Top-10 global diversified miner by market cap; top-tier producer of premium (high-Fe) iron ore via Kumba and Minas-Rio; mid-tier global copper producer (~700-760kt/yr guidance) set to become materially larger and more copper-weighted post-Teck merger; De Beers remains one of the largest rough diamond producers by value alongside ALROSA, though structurally challenged by lab-grown competition and weak demand

moat_factors.description: Collahuasi, Los Bronces, Quellaveco and Kumba/Minas-Rio are first-quartile cost-curve, large-scale, long-life assets that are extremely difficult and capital-intensive to replicate
Kumba and Minas-Rio produce high-Fe, low-impurity iron ore that commands a price premium from steelmakers seeking lower emissions intensity

moat_factors.factor: De Beers brand and historic distribution control (Sightholder system)
moat_factors.description: Long-standing control over rough diamond grading/distribution gives De Beers pricing influence, though this moat is eroding due to lab-grown diamonds and weak Chinese/US demand
The Collahuasi/Quebrada Blanca adjacency with Teck is expected to generate ~$800m pre-tax recurring synergies plus $1.4bn EBITDA uplift, a genuine structural cost advantage once realized
Decades-long permitting timelines for new copper and iron ore mines favor incumbents with existing permitted, infrastructure-connected assets

weaknesses: No pricing power over commodity outputs - a pure price-taker in copper, iron ore and (increasingly) diamonds
Heavy reliance on a small number of flagship assets (Collahuasi, Los Bronces, Quellaveco, Kumba, Minas-Rio) concentrates operational risk
De Beers has lost structural pricing power to lab-grown diamonds and is being sold at a loss after repeated impairments
Complex, multi-year portfolio restructuring (PGMs demerger, Steelmaking Coal, Nickel, De Beers divestitures, Teck merger) creates significant execution and distraction risk
South Africa operational base (Kumba, Samancor, De Beers legacy) exposed to rail/port logistics constraints, power supply issues and political/regulatory uncertainty

growth_drivers: Merger with Teck Resources to form 'Anglo Teck' - expected to close by March 2027 (China antitrust approval is the final outstanding milestone), creating one of the world's largest copper producers with >70% copper EBITDA exposure and the Collahuasi/Quebrada Blanca adjacency synergy ($800m pre-tax recurring synergies plus $1.4bn underlying EBITDA uplift)

Woodsmith polyhalite project (UK) and Sakatti (Finland, EU-designated Strategic Project, March 2025) as the next generation of FutureSmart Mining growth projects, diversifying into crop nutrients and new-economy minerals
Quellaveco (Peru) expansion studies to lift production above the ~300kt/yr run rate, plus ongoing supergene-to-hypogene transition planning to smooth production into the 2030s
Secular copper demand tailwinds from electrification, EV adoption and decarbonisation, and premium iron ore demand from steelmakers decarbonising via lower-emission feedstock

$1.8 billion run-rate cost-out program (achieved in FY2025) continuing to support margins; further operational excellence/Lean/AI-enabled productivity initiatives (Assisted Core Logging, AI Centre of Excellence)

Portfolio simplification is itself a value-unlock catalyst: proceeds from Valterra Platinum residual stake ($2.5bn), Steelmaking Coal sale (up to $3.875bn) and Nickel sale (up to $500m) are being used to delever and fund the simplified, higher-margin copper/iron ore/crop nutrients portfolio

business.description: Revenue and margins are directly exposed to volatile LME copper, iron ore index and diamond price swings with no hedging of the bulk of exposure

A handful of flagship mines (Collahuasi, Los Bronces, Quellaveco, Kumba, Minas-Rio) generate the large majority of EBITDA; weather events (record Chile snowfall/rainfall in 2026), grade decline or operational outages at any one asset materially move group results

Lab-grown diamond competition and weak Chinese/US demand have driven diamond price indices down ~18% YTD 2026 and realised prices down 37%; De Beers has required repeated multi-billion-dollar impairments ($2.3bn in FY2025 alone) and a two-year production pause at Venetia

business.risk: Water availability and permitting in Chile
business.description: El Soldado and Collahuasi face drought risk and a May 2026 Chilean Environmental Tribunal ruling partially set aside the desalination plant's Environmental Authorization, forcing reliance on alternative water sources

financial.description: Net debt was $8.2bn at June 2026 (1.0x net debt/EBITDA), down from $8.6bn at FY2025, but completion timing of Steelmaking Coal, Nickel and De Beers sales affects the pace of further deleveraging ahead of the Teck merger
Costs are incurred in CLP, PEN, BRL and ZAR against USD revenue; unit cost guidance is explicitly FX-rate dependent (c.900 CLP:USD, c.3.4 PEN:USD, c.5.2 BRL:USD, c.16.50 ZAR:USD for 2026)

Repeated De Beers carrying-value write-downs and discontinued-operations remeasurements (e.g., the Steelmaking Coal carrying-value reduction to reflect the Dhilmar sale terms) depress attributable earnings and could recur

regulatory.description: China's antitrust regulator approval is explicitly flagged by management as the final outstanding regulatory milestone for the Anglo Teck merger; delay or conditions could push completion beyond the March 2027 target

The MMG nickel sale faces a European Commission statement of objections over European stainless-steel ferronickel supply and a Brazilian competition authority probe, with the deal deadline already extended once

Botswana owns 15% of De Beers and 50% of Debswana and holds pre-emptive rights over any De Beers sale; it could choose to partner with, or pre-empt, the preferred bidder (reportedly the Gareth Penny-linked Global Diamond Consortium), adding uncertainty to deal structure and timing
Kumba, Samancor and legacy South African operations remain subject to South African mining, labour, BEE/ownership and environmental regulation

macro.description: Management repeatedly cites 'slow economic recovery in China' and weak Chinese demand as a drag on both industrial metals (steel/iron ore) and diamond demand
Chair's statement flags 'emerging international trade restrictions' and geopolitical uncertainty as a factor expected to persist into 2026/2027
Energy input cost volatility and higher ocean freight rates are cited as pressuring controllable costs and iron ore spot price realisations in 2026

execution.description: Simultaneous execution of the PGMs demerger (completed), Steelmaking Coal sale, Nickel sale, De Beers separation and the transformational Teck merger creates significant management distraction and integration risk over 2025-2027

Peabody walked away from the original Steelmaking Coal sale agreement in 2025 (now in arbitration), forcing Anglo to re-run the process and ultimately sell to Dhilmar on revised terms - a precedent for execution risk on the still-pending De Beers and Nickel sales

Realizing the claimed $800m synergies and $1.4bn EBITDA uplift from the Collahuasi/Quebrada Blanca adjacency depends on successful post-merger integration of two large, previously independent organizations

macro_factors.industry_outlook: Diversified mining sector outlook is bifurcated: copper demand/pricing is structurally supported by electrification and AI/data-centre-driven power demand (2026 YTD copper realized price up ~40% YoY), while iron ore faces softer pricing on weak Chinese steel demand (FOB prices down ~11% YTD 2026) and diamonds are in a cyclical and structural downturn (price index down ~18%, realized prices down ~37% YTD 2026) from lab-grown competition and weak luxury demand in China/US
macro_factors.cyclicality: High - revenue and earnings are directly tied to global commodity price cycles and Chinese industrial demand; De Beers specifically is also exposed to discretionary consumer luxury spending cycles
macro_factors.interest_rate_sensitivity: Moderate - large capital projects (Woodsmith, Quellaveco expansion) and elevated net debt mean financing costs matter, though net debt/EBITDA of ~1.0x is currently manageable

recent_developments.event: Q3 2026 production report: copper down 5% YoY (174.9kt) on record Chile snowfall and lower-grade stockpile ore at Collahuasi; premium iron ore down 4% on Kumba UHDMS tie-in; diamonds down 11%; FY2026 guidance maintained, with Copper Peru unit cost guidance improved to ~50c/lb (from ~65c/lb) and De Beers 2026 production guidance raised to 25-28 Mct (from 21-26 Mct)
Management confirms China antitrust approval is the final outstanding regulatory milestone for the Anglo Teck merger, with completion by March 2027 unchanged

H1 2026 interim results: continuing-operations revenue $9.9bn (+11%), underlying EBITDA $4.0bn (+35%), EBITDA margin 38%; loss attributable to equity shareholders of $0.9bn (narrowed from $1.9bn in H1 2025), reflecting a carrying-value reduction on Steelmaking Coal to match the agreed Dhilmar sale terms; net debt reduced to $8.2bn (1.0x EBITDA); interim dividend $0.23/share (vs $0.07 prior year, 40% payout policy)
De Beers announced a two-year production pause at its flagship Venetia mine (South Africa, ~10% of De Beers output) to cut costs amid collapsing rough diamond prices and lab-grown competition

Agreed sale of the Australian Steelmaking Coal business to Dhilmar Ltd for up to $3.875bn (US$2.3bn upfront plus up to $1.575bn price-linked earnout), replacing the collapsed Peabody deal; expected to complete by Q1 2027; Anglo continues arbitration against Peabody over the failed original transaction

De Beers sale process progressed: Anglo reportedly selected a preferred bidder (the Gareth Penny-linked 'Global Diamond Consortium') from three shortlisted bidders; Botswana (15% De Beers shareholder, 50% Debswana partner) retains pre-emptive rights and is weighing whether to partner with or pre-empt the chosen bidder; sale targeted for completion in Q4 2026/subject to Botswana government approval
Anglo American and Teck shareholders approved the merger of equals (Anglo Teck); Government of Canada granted Investment Canada Act approval; competition clearances secured in Canada and Australia

Anglo American received renewed takeover interest from BHP regarding a combination of the two companies; the Board reviewed the proposal and BHP subsequently announced it was no longer considering it (echoing BHP's failed 2024 takeover approach)
Monetised the residual 19.9% stake in Valterra Platinum (formerly Anglo American Platinum, demerged May 2025) for $2.5bn in cash

Announced the merger of equals with Teck Resources to form Anglo Teck, targeting >70% copper revenue exposure, ~$800m pre-tax recurring synergies and a further $1.4bn underlying EBITDA uplift from the Collahuasi/Quebrada Blanca adjacency

items.notes: Chile and Peru both weighted to H2 2026 (Chile on water availability, Peru on grade profile)

items.target: ~139 c/lb group-wide (Peru improved to ~50c/lb from ~65c/lb; Chile unchanged at ~210c/lb)
items.notes: Peru improvement driven by strong by-product (molybdenum) credits and cost control; FX assumptions ~900 CLP:USD, ~3.4 PEN:USD
Kumba weighted to H1 2026 ahead of UHDMS tie-in in H2; sales unaffected by stockpile drawdown
Pressured by higher ocean freight rates and energy cost volatility affecting spot price realisations
Unit cost revised to ~$70/carat (from ~$80/carat); follows the Venetia production pause and De Beers' management actions to align output with weak demand
Cited as a key driver of FY2025 margin resilience and the 35% H1 2026 EBITDA growth
China antitrust clearance is the final outstanding regulatory milestone; integration planning described as 'advanced stage'
Dhilmar transaction; subject to competition/regulatory clearances and pre-emption arrangements
FY2025 final dividend $0.16/share (total $0.23/share for FY2025); H1 2026 interim dividend $0.23/share, up from $0.07/share in H1 2025

guidance.management_commentary: CEO Duncan Wanblad: operational performance was 'resilient' in Q3 2026 despite extreme Chile winter weather, with the business 'on track to meet 2026 guidance' aided by expected Q4 copper grade improvement. He describes the Teck merger as 'progressing' with integration planning 'at an advanced stage' and reiterates the March 2027 completion target, flagging China's antitrust review as the final gating item. On De Beers, management says it continues to 'work towards a transaction in a challenging market, having taken decisive action to protect cash and preserve value' (referencing the Venetia pause and capex rephasing). The Chair's statement notes 2025 was a 'highly consequential year' for portfolio transformation and expects 'similar themes' (slow China recovery, trade-policy uncertainty, geopolitics) to persist in 2026/2027.

bull_case: The Teck merger (expected to close by March 2027) creates a global top-tier, >70%-copper-exposed miner with genuine, quantified synergies (~$800m pre-tax recurring, plus ~$1.4bn EBITDA uplift from the Collahuasi/Quebrada Blanca adjacency) at a moment when copper prices are up ~40% YoY on electrification/AI power demand tailwinds

Portfolio simplification is de-risking and refocusing the business onto first-quartile cost-curve, long-life copper and premium iron ore assets, while proceeds from PGMs, Steelmaking Coal and Nickel divestitures fund deleveraging (net debt down to $8.2bn, 1.0x EBITDA, from $10.6bn)

H1 2026 showed strong operating momentum (continuing-operations EBITDA +35% YoY, 38% margin) with the $1.8bn cost-out program fully realized and still-improving unit costs (Peru copper cost guidance cut to ~50c/lb)
Woodsmith and Sakatti provide multi-decade, counter-cyclical growth optionality in crop nutrients/new-economy minerals beyond the base-metals cycle
Repeated takeover interest from BHP (2024 and again in late 2025) signals that strategic/financial acquirers see embedded value in the asset base that the market may not be fully pricing
bear_case: De Beers remains a persistent drag - repeated multi-billion-dollar impairments, a two-year Venetia production pause, and a diamond market in both cyclical and structural (lab-grown) decline, with no signed sale agreement yet and Botswana's pre-emptive rights adding deal uncertainty into late 2026

Execution risk is unusually high and concentrated in a short window: simultaneous completion of the Steelmaking Coal sale, Nickel sale (facing EU antitrust objections and a Brazilian competition probe), De Beers separation and the transformational Teck merger (still awaiting China antitrust clearance) all need to land successfully by Q1 2027
Precedent for failed divestitures exists - Peabody's 2025 withdrawal from the original Steelmaking Coal deal (now in arbitration) shows these processes can unravel even after an agreement is signed
Heavy exposure to Chinese industrial and consumer demand (iron ore, diamonds) leaves the group vulnerable if China's economic recovery remains slow, as management itself flags for 2026/2027

Operational concentration risk is real and recurring - extreme weather in Chile (record snowfall/rainfall in 2026) and water/permitting constraints at Collahuasi/El Soldado repeatedly dent copper output, showing the flagship assets are not immune to physical and regulatory disruption
